- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike (≥ 5% from prior day) and sentiment is neutral or negative, expect overshoot; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days falling from 70+), model often lags; adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lag in downward movement.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.15) and model is flat or rising, model underestimates; add 2–4% to forecast for next 3–7 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price by 1–3% when sentiment is volatile (±0.15+ in last 5 days); apply +1.5% bias correction.  
- If sentiment history shows recent accumulation of positive sentiment (e.g., 3+ days > 0.3), model often fails to capture momentum; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5 days.
